# Quantum groups, q-oscillators and defects {#sec-defect-qg}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Know what a topological defect of a conformal field theory is, how Verlinde lines act on states and fuse, and how chiral perturbations turn topological defects into integrable massive ones.
- Understand why a Borel subalgebra of $U_q(\hat g)$, a Hopf subalgebra rather than a coideal, is a natural setting for a transmitting defect, and prove that its intertwiners solve the triangle relation under a Hom-dimension and normalization hypothesis.
- Work with the $q$-oscillator algebra and its Weyl and Fock modules, and obtain from the universal R-matrix both the sine-Gordon transmission matrices and the L-operator of Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov.
- Build defect operators on the circle, relate them to Baxter's Q-operators, and read their TQ relations as the defect bootstrap of @sec-sg-defect-spectrum in operator form.
- Compare, entry by entry, the algebraic structures behind boundaries and defects.
:::

@sec-boundary-qg found reflection matrices in two steps: identify the charges that survive a boundary, and solve the linear equations that say the reflection matrix commutes with them. This chapter does the same for transmission. The surviving charges now generate a Borel subalgebra $U_q(\mathfrak b^\pm)$ of $U_q(\hat g)$, generated by the $k_j$ and either all $e_j$ or all $f_j$. Unlike the coideals of the boundary, a Borel subalgebra is a Hopf subalgebra, which is what the argument for a line that particles cross from either side uses. Its representations on the defect space $\mathcal W$ are infinite dimensional, and they are representations of the $q$-oscillator algebra that Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov used to construct Q-operators [@blz1997]. Defects and Q-operators are thus two readings of the same algebra: transmission matrices are L-operators, and defect operators on the circle are transfer matrices with an infinite-dimensional auxiliary space [@weston2010; @cz2011].

We work in the conventions of Part VI: $\Delta(e_j)=e_j\otimes1+k_j\otimes e_j$, $\Delta(f_j)=f_j\otimes k_j^{-1}+1\otimes f_j$, $q=-e^{-i\pi\lambda}$ for sine-Gordon (-@eq-q-physical), $y=e^{\lambda\theta}$, $y_d=e^{\lambda\theta_d}$, and $\kappa=q-q^{-1}$. The transmission matrix $\mathbb T(\theta):V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W\to\mathcal W\otimes V(\theta)$ and $\mathbb L=P\,\mathbb T$ are as in @sec-triangle-relations, and $v_+$ is the soliton. The numerical checks are in `textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py` (16 checks, about 90 s) and `textbook_code/defect_transfer.py` (9 checks, about 30 s).

## Topological defects in conformal field theory {#sec-cft-topological-defects}

**Topological defects.** Place a conformal field theory on a cylinder and wrap a defect line of type $a$ around it. The line becomes an operator $D_a$ on the space of states $\mathcal H$. The defect is **conformal** if $T-\bar T$ is continuous across it, and **topological**, or purely transmitting, if $T$ and $\bar T$ are separately continuous:
$$
[L_m,D_a]=[\bar L_m,D_a]=0\qquad\text{for all }m .
$$
Then the line can be deformed freely without changing correlators, two lines can be brought together without singularity, and their product $D_aD_b$ is again a sum of defect operators: topological defects form a **fusion algebra** [@petkova_zuber2001; @ffrs2007; @runkel2008]. In the massive theories of this part, energy and momentum conservation at the defect (@prp-defect-momentum) is the remnant of this condition.

**Twisted partition functions.** Petkova and Zuber classified topological defects by the twisted partition functions they produce [@petkova_zuber2001]. For a diagonal rational theory, $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_i R_i\otimes\bar R_i$ with each irreducible $R_i\otimes\bar R_i$ of the chiral algebras occurring once, an operator that commutes with both chiral algebras defining the irreducible modules $R_i$, $\bar R_i$ is, by Schur's lemma, a number on each summand. Inserting it in a torus partition function and demanding that the crossed channel, in which the defect runs along time and the states live on a circle cut by it, has non-negative integer multiplicities is a consistency condition of Cardy type [@petkova_zuber2001, eq. (4.8)]. Its basic solutions are the **Verlinde lines**, one for each representation $a$,
$$
D_a=\sum_i\frac{S_{ai}}{S_{0i}}\,P_i ,\qquad D_aD_b=\sum_cN_{ab}^{\;c}D_c ,
$$
with $S$ the modular matrix, $P_i$ the projector onto $R_i\otimes\bar R_i$, $0$ the vacuum and $N_{ab}^{\;c}$ the fusion coefficients. In the crossed channel the space of states on a circle cut by $D_a$ contains $R_i\otimes\bar R_j$ with multiplicity $N_{ij}^{\;a}$, for self-conjugate representations [@petkova_zuber2001, eqs. (4.5), (5.1)]. The fusion rule follows from the Verlinde formula, since $i\mapsto S_{ai}/S_{0i}$ is a character of the fusion algebra. The projectors $P_i$ play the role of Ishibashi states, and the integrality condition that of Cardy's condition for boundaries [@petkova_zuber2001, Secs. 3–4].

**Ising: symmetry and duality.** The critical Ising model has the three Verlinde lines $\mathbb 1$, $\varepsilon$, $\sigma$. With the modular matrix of the Ising model, $D_\varepsilon$ is $+1$ on the sectors of $\mathbb 1$ and $\varepsilon$ and $-1$ on that of $\sigma$: it is the line of the $\mathbb Z_2$ spin flip, a line of antiferromagnetic bonds on the lattice. $D_\sigma$ is $\sqrt2$, $-\sqrt2$, $0$ on the sectors of $\mathbb 1$, $\varepsilon$, $\sigma$, and $\sigma\times\sigma=\mathbb 1+\varepsilon$. Fröhlich, Fuchs, Runkel and Schweigert showed that $\sigma$ is the **Kramers–Wannier duality defect**: dragging it past a spin field turns it into a disorder field attached to an $\varepsilon$-line, and past an energy field it changes its sign, so a small $\sigma$-loop around a correlator of spins proves its equality with the dual correlator of disorder fields [@ffrs2004]. A line that fuses with its conjugate to more than the identity is **non-invertible**; in modern language the topological lines are generalized symmetries, and @sec-topological-lines described their imprint on S-matrices [@cck2024]. In general rational theories the defects, their fusion and their action on fields follow from a three-dimensional topological field theory [@ffrs2007].

**Lee–Yang.** The minimal model $\mathcal M(2,5)$ has two Verlinde lines, $\mathbb 1$ and $\Phi$, with $\Phi\times\Phi=\mathbb 1+\Phi$. $D_\Phi$ acts on the two sectors by the two roots of $d^2=d+1$: $\frac{1-\sqrt5}2$ on the vacuum module and $\frac{1+\sqrt5}2$ on the module of weight $-\frac15$. These are the conformal defects of @sec-defect-lee-yang, and the perturbed defect $\Phi$ carries the transmission factor (-@eq-ly-transmission).

**The free boson.** For the compactified free boson, behind sine-Gordon theory, the topological defects include the lines of the two $U(1)$ symmetries. The line of the winding symmetry is $e^{i\alpha T}$, with $T$ the topological charge, and it commutes with the sine-Gordon perturbation $\cos\beta_{\rm SG}\phi$; it is the conformal ancestor of the twist defect of @prp-twist-defect. A second family of topological defects glues the two sides by a reflection of one chirality. The massless limit of the type-I$_-$ defect conditions (-@eq-sg-defect-conditions) is of this kind: at $m_0=0$ they read $\partial_x\phi=\partial_t\psi$, $\partial_x\psi=\partial_t\phi$, and with $\phi=\phi_L(x^+)+\phi_R(x^-)$, $x^\pm=t\pm x$, and the same for $\psi$, they are equivalent to
$$
\psi_L=\phi_L,\qquad\psi_R=-\phi_R+\text{const}\qquad\text{at }x=0 .
$$ {#eq-dq-massless-defect}
Left-movers pass unchanged and right-movers change sign, so $\psi$ continues the dual field $\phi_L-\phi_R$ of $\phi$ (by hand, @exr-dq-chiral-defect). These are local gluing conditions. For a compact boson a defect must also respect the lattice of momenta and windings: with $p_{L,R}=n/R\pm wR$, reflecting $p_R$ maps $(n,w)$ to $(R^2w,n/R^2)$, which leaves the lattice unless $R^2=1$. So the reflection of one chirality is naturally a T-duality interface between the radii $R$ and $1/R$, and realizing it as a line within one compactified theory needs compatible radii and lattice data. We use the local gluing only to identify the chiral fields.

## Perturbed defects and their charges {#sec-perturbed-defects}

**Chiral defect perturbations.** As in @sec-boundary-cpt, regard the imaginary-coupling theory as a conformal field theory perturbed by a bulk field $\Phi=\Phi_L\Phi_R$, the product of a chiral and an antichiral field. Konik and LeClair proposed perturbing a topological defect by a defect field of one chirality, $g\int dt\,\Phi_L(0,t)$ [@konik_leclair1999, eq. (2.7)]. If $J_L$ and $J_R$ are the chiral parts of a bulk conserved current, the first-order change of $J_L$ across the defect is the integrated operator product of $J_L$ with $\Phi_L$. When its simple-pole residue is a total derivative $\partial H_L$, as integrability of the bulk requires, the image-delta identity (-@eq-image-delta) turns it into a contact term [@konik_leclair1999, eqs. (2.8)–(2.10)]:
$$
J_L(0^+,t)-J_L(0^-,t)=4\pi ig\,\partial_tH_L,\qquad J_R(0^+,t)-J_R(0^-,t)=0 .
$$
So the charge $\int J_L+4\pi gH_L$ is conserved with a defect term, and $\int J_R$ without one. For the energy–momentum tensor both energy and momentum survive, and the defect is purely transmitting. The defect parameters enter as couplings, and their relation to $\theta_d$ is dynamical (@cnj-defect-parameter).

**The Lagrangian defect at the conformal point.** By (-@eq-dq-massless-defect), $\phi+\psi=2\phi_L+\text{const}$ and $\phi-\psi=2\phi_R+\text{const}$ at the defect. The two terms of the sine-Gordon defect potential (-@eq-sg-defect-potential),
$$
\sigma\cos\frac{\beta_{\rm SG}(\phi+\psi)}2\qquad\text{and}\qquad\sigma^{-1}\cos\frac{\beta_{\rm SG}(\phi-\psi)}2 ,
$$
are therefore chiral defect fields of opposite chiralities, with couplings proportional to $m_0\sigma$ and $m_0\sigma^{-1}$. Their product is fixed by the bulk coupling $m_0^2$, and a boost rescales them oppositely, which is why $\sigma=e^{-\theta_d}$ behaves like a rapidity. This is the structure found in conformal perturbation theory for the Lee–Yang defect, where the bulk coupling is the product of the chiral and antichiral defect couplings [@bhw2014], and for the perturbed minimal-model defects of Runkel below [@runkel2010, eq. (1.20)]. The two limits of @prp-defect-twist-limit, left-movers passing with a phase and right-movers converted, are the two halves of (-@eq-dq-massless-defect).

**T-systems.** Runkel studied the operators $D_a(\lambda\varphi)$ of topological defects perturbed by a chiral defect field $\varphi$, wound around the cylinder [@runkel2008]. In the minimal model $\mathcal M(p,p')$ the defects $(1,s)$ carry a chiral field of weight $h_{1,3}=2p/p'-1$, and for $p/p'<3/4$ no regularization is needed. The perturbed defect operators commute with each other and with $L_0+\bar L_0$, and they satisfy [@runkel2008, eqs. (1.1)–(1.3)]
$$
D_{(1,s)}(q\lambda\varphi)\,D_{(1,s)}(q^{-1}\lambda\varphi)=\mathrm{id}+D_{(1,s-1)}(\lambda\varphi)\,D_{(1,s+1)}(\lambda\varphi),\qquad q=e^{\pi ip/p'} ,
$$
the T-system of fused transfer matrices. The mechanism is fusion: $(1,2)\star(1,s)=(1,s-1)+(1,s+1)$, and the relative coupling can be tuned so that the defect-changing fields between the two summands drop out. The $D_{(1,s)}$ are cousins of the T-operators of Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov (@sec-q-operators), which act on chiral representations only.

**Non-local charges from defects.** With chiral and antichiral perturbations $\lambda\varphi_s+\tilde\lambda\bar\varphi_s$ on the $(1,s)$ defect, Runkel showed for $p/p'<\frac12$ that the defect operators $D_s(\lambda,\tilde\lambda)$ commute with the Hamiltonian of the bulk theory perturbed by $\Phi_{1,3}$ with coupling $\xi\lambda\tilde\lambda$, commute with each other when $\lambda\tilde\lambda$ is fixed, satisfy the T-system with $\lambda\to q^{\pm1}\lambda$, $\tilde\lambda\to q^{\mp1}\tilde\lambda$, and, fused onto the Cardy boundary $(1,1)$, give the perturbed boundary $(1,s)$ [@runkel2010, eqs. (1.15)–(1.22)]. The one free parameter $\lambda/\tilde\lambda$ is the spectral parameter of a family of non-local conserved charges, in the sense of BLZ: defect operators are the generating functions of non-local charges of the massive theory. As operators they are, for now, formal power series in the couplings [@runkel2010, Sec. 1].

**Which non-local charges survive.** The non-local charges $Q_j$, $\bar Q_j$ of @sec-nonlocal-charges are built from left- and right-moving vertex operators, and $Q_j\to e_j$, $\bar Q_jq^{-T_j}\to f_j$, $q^{T_j}\to k_j$. A defect perturbed by a field of a single chirality leaves the currents of the other chirality continuous, and it carries topological charge, so the charges of the other chirality and $q^{T_j}$, with the defect contributing to $T_j$, commute with it. These generate a Borel subalgebra: $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)=\langle f_j,k_j^{\pm1}\rangle$ when the perturbation is left-moving, $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)=\langle e_j,k_j^{\pm1}\rangle$ when it is right-moving. For the charges of the same chirality the argument above produces, at first order, defect terms that change the defect state, and it does not decide whether they survive. The exact transmission matrices decide it: the type-I$_-$ matrix of @sec-sg-transmission-matrix intertwines $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$, and for generic $q$ its Weyl module does not extend to all of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$. The weights force $e_1|n\rangle=c_n|n+1\rangle$; the relation $[e_1,f_0]=0$, with $f_0$ a constant upward shift, forces $c_n$ to be constant; then $e_1$ commutes with the constant downward shift $f_1$, contradicting $[e_1,f_1]=(k_1-k_1^{-1})/\kappa$. (Numerically, no action of the $e_j$ on $\mathcal W$ is intertwined by $\mathbb T$ with the Hopf coproduct; the best candidate leaves a residual of 0.88, `textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`.) Twisted by charge conjugation they do survive, with $\mathcal W$ carrying a second module structure: on the particle that has crossed the defect, $e_j$ acts as $e_{\tau(j)}$, with $\tau$ the exchange of the two nodes (@prp-diagonal-borel). The exact transmission matrices therefore realize the Borel symmetry, as the classical theory anticipated through the Weyl-type Poisson algebra of the defect values (@prp-defect-involution). The first-order conformal argument motivates this but does not construct the all-orders massive charges, and we do not claim a classification of all possible defect symmetries.

## Borel subalgebras and q-oscillators {#sec-borel}

**Why a Hopf subalgebra.** For a boundary, the boundary is always the last tensor factor, and a left coideal, $\Delta(B)\subset U_q(\hat g)\otimes B$, is exactly what acts there (@sec-coideal). A defect sits between particles: in $V_1\otimes\mathcal W\otimes V_2$, which occurs halfway through the triangle relation, the iterated coproduct acts on $\mathcal W$ through the middle leg, and the argument of @thm-t-triangle needs both legs of the coproduct to stay in the algebra represented on the defect. A Hopf subalgebra provides this; a single left coideal does not. This makes Hopf subalgebras a sufficient setting, not a classification of all possible transmitting-defect symmetries. The Borel subalgebras
$$
U_q(\mathfrak b^+)=\langle e_j,k_j^{\pm1}\rangle,\qquad U_q(\mathfrak b^-)=\langle f_j,k_j^{\pm1}\rangle
$$
are Hopf subalgebras, since $\Delta(e_j)$ and $\Delta(f_j)$ involve only $e_j$ or $f_j$ and $k_j^{\pm1}$. Their relations are those of $k_j$ with $e_j$ (or $f_j$) and the $q$-Serre relations; there is no relation between $e_j$ and $f_j$ to satisfy, which is why they have modules that $U_q(\hat g)$ does not. Unless a root-of-unity specialization is stated, we assume from here on that $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ is not a root of unity, and we fix the powers $q^s$; at roots of unity the modules below become reducible and further intertwiners appear.

**The $q$-oscillator algebra.** For $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ these modules come from the $q$-oscillator algebra $\mathcal A_q$, generated by $\mathsf a_\pm$ and $q^{\pm\mathsf h}$ with
$$
q\,\mathsf a_+\mathsf a_--q^{-1}\mathsf a_-\mathsf a_+=\frac1{q-q^{-1}},\qquad q^{\mathsf h}\,\mathsf a_\pm\,q^{-\mathsf h}=q^{\pm2}\mathsf a_\pm ,
$$ {#eq-q-oscillator}
in the normalization of Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov [@blz1997, eq. (2.27)] [@blz1999, eq. (3.8)]. The element $Z=\mathsf a_+\mathsf a_--\kappa^{-2}$ satisfies $\mathsf a_-\mathsf a_+-\kappa^{-2}=q^2Z$ and $Z\mathsf a_\pm=q^{\pm2}\mathsf a_\pm Z$, so it generates a two-sided ideal. The maps
$$
U_q(\mathfrak b^+):\ e_1\mapsto iy_W\,\mathsf a_+,\ \ e_0\mapsto iy_W\,\mathsf a_-;\qquad U_q(\mathfrak b^-):\ f_1\mapsto\frac i{y_W}\,\mathsf a_-,\ \ f_0\mapsto\frac i{y_W}\,\mathsf a_+;\qquad k_1\mapsto q^{\mathsf h}=k_0^{-1}
$$
are homomorphisms. The $q$-Serre relations hold because $e_1e_0$ and $e_0e_1$ are affine functions of $Z$, which $q$-commutes with $\mathsf a_\pm$ (@exr-dq-oscillator); we also checked them on the modules below (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`). The parameter $y_W$ is a spectral parameter of the module. Level zero, $k_0k_1=1$, is forced: with $k_0k_1\ne1$ on $\mathcal W$ there is no transmission matrix (@prp-sg-t-unique).

**Weyl modules.** On the quotient $Z=0$ the oscillators are invertible up to a constant, $\mathsf a_+\mathsf a_-=\mathsf a_-\mathsf a_+=\kappa^{-2}$. Its irreducible representations are the Weyl modules
$$
\mathcal W=\mathrm{span}\{|n\rangle,\ n\in\mathbb Z\},\qquad \mathsf a_\pm|n\rangle=\frac{|n\pm1\rangle}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad q^{\mathsf h}|n\rangle=q^{2n+s}|n\rangle .
$$ {#eq-weyl-module}
Through the homomorphisms they are the module $\mathcal W^-(y_d)$ of $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ of @sec-sg-transmission-matrix and its analogue $\mathcal W^+(y_d)$ for $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$, with $y_W=y_d$: $e_1|n\rangle=\mu y_d|n+1\rangle$, $e_0|n\rangle=\mu y_d|n-1\rangle$, respectively $f_1|n\rangle=\frac\mu{y_d}|n-1\rangle$, $f_0|n\rangle=\frac\mu{y_d}|n+1\rangle$, with $\mu=i/(q-q^{-1})$. The label $2n+s$ is the topological charge of the defect. There is no highest or lowest weight, as befits a defect whose jump can be any multiple of $2\pi/\beta_{\rm SG}$.

**Fock modules.** The standard representation of (-@eq-q-oscillator) has a vacuum annihilated by $\mathsf a_-$:
$$
\mathcal F=\mathrm{span}\{|n\rangle,\ n\ge0\},\qquad \mathsf a_+|n\rangle=\frac{|n+1\rangle}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad \mathsf a_-|n\rangle=\frac{1-q^{2n}}{q-q^{-1}}\,|n-1\rangle,\qquad q^{\mathsf h}|n\rangle=q^{2n+s}|n\rangle ,
$$ {#eq-fock-module}
on which $Z|n\rangle=-\kappa^{-2}q^{2n}|n\rangle$. Through the homomorphisms it gives the Fock modules $\mathcal F^\pm(y_F)$ of the two Borel subalgebras; $\mathcal F^+$ is the kind of representation used by Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov for their Q-operators (@sec-q-operators). More generally, for a module of $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ on which $e_1$ shifts $n$ up and $e_0$ shifts it down, the $q$-Serre relations hold if and only if $u_n=e_1e_0|_n$ has the form $A+Bq^{2n}+Cq^{-2n}$, since $u_n-[3]u_{n+1}+[3]u_{n+2}-u_{n+3}=0$ (checked numerically, with a failing control). Weyl modules have $B=C=0$; the Fock modules of the $q$-oscillator have $C=0$ and $A+B=0$, so that $u_0=0$ and the module truncates; the generalized oscillator modules of Rossi and Weston, which give the type-II defects of @sec-type-two, have $B,C\ne0$ [@rossi_weston2002; @weston2010].

## Transmission matrices as intertwiners {#sec-t-intertwiner}

A transmission matrix of a defect with symmetry $U_q(\mathfrak b)$, $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak b^+$ or $\mathfrak b^-$, commutes with it:
$$
\mathbb T(\theta)\,(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho)\Delta(b)=(\rho\otimes\pi_\theta)\Delta(b)\,\mathbb T(\theta)\qquad\text{for all }b\in U_q(\mathfrak b),
$$ {#eq-borel-intertwiner}
with $\pi_\theta$ the representation on $V(\theta)$ and $\rho$ that on $\mathcal W$. The same coproduct appears on both sides, because tensor order is spatial order. The equation is linear, the defect analogue of Jimbo's equations (-@eq-jimbo) and of (-@eq-k-intertwiner).

::: {#thm-t-triangle}
## Intertwiners solve the triangle relation
**[Theorem]** Let $\mathcal W$ be a $U_q(\mathfrak b)$-module. Suppose that (i) $\mathbb T(\theta)$ satisfies (-@eq-borel-intertwiner) for all $\theta$; (ii) for generic $\theta_1,\theta_2$ the space of $U_q(\mathfrak b)$-intertwiners $V(\theta_1)\otimes V(\theta_2)\otimes\mathcal W\to\mathcal W\otimes V(\theta_2)\otimes V(\theta_1)$, with $U_q(\mathfrak b)$ acting by the iterated coproduct, is one-dimensional; and (iii) the two sides of (-@eq-triangle-braid) agree on one matrix element that is nonzero for generic parameters. Then $\mathbb T$ satisfies the triangle relation (-@eq-triangle-braid), with the $\check R$ of @sec-trigonometric-r.
:::

::: {.proof}
Both sides of (-@eq-triangle-braid) map $V(\theta_1)\otimes V(\theta_2)\otimes\mathcal W$ to $\mathcal W\otimes V(\theta_2)\otimes V(\theta_1)$, and each factor commutes with the action of $U_q(\mathfrak b)$. For $\check R$ this holds because it intertwines $\Delta(a)$ for every $a\in U_q(\hat g)$, in particular for the components of $\Delta(b)$. For $\mathbb T_{23}$, write $\Delta^{(2)}(b)=(1\otimes\Delta)\Delta(b)=\sum b_{(1)}\otimes\Delta(b_{(2)})$; since $U_q(\mathfrak b)$ is a Hopf subalgebra, $b_{(2)}\in U_q(\mathfrak b)$, and $\mathbb T$ intertwines $\Delta(b_{(2)})$ by (i). For $\mathbb T_{12}$, which acts on $V(\theta_1)\otimes\mathcal W\otimes V(\theta_2)$, use $\Delta^{(2)}(b)=\sum\Delta(b_{(1)})\otimes b_{(2)}$ in the same way. Coassociativity makes the two decompositions agree. So both sides are intertwiners, and by (ii) they are proportional; (iii) fixes the constant.
:::

Condition (iii) is a genuine check, not a choice of normalization: rescaling $\mathbb T(\theta_1)$, $\mathbb T(\theta_2)$ or $\check R$ by scalar functions multiplies both sides of (-@eq-triangle-braid) by the same factor. And agreement on a matrix element that vanishes would fix nothing. The closure of both coproduct legs used in the proof is sufficient; we do not claim that every symmetry of a transmitting defect must be of this kind.

The Hopf property was used for $\mathbb T_{12}$, where $\mathcal W$ sits in the middle, and this is the step that fails for a coideal (@exr-dq-hopf). Hypothesis (ii) is the real content, as for @thm-k-reflection. A truncated window of a bilateral module can create or remove intertwiners, so we checked it in two ways (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`). On windows of the defect space, the intertwiners $V(y_1)\otimes V(y_2)\otimes\mathcal W\to\mathcal W\otimes V(y_2)\otimes V(y_1)$ form a one-dimensional space for the Weyl modules of both Borel subalgebras and for the Fock module $\mathcal F^+$. Without truncation, exactly at a generic rational point: composing with an invertible product of local intertwiners identifies this space with the endomorphisms of $V(y_1)\otimes V(y_2)\otimes\mathcal W$. On the Weyl modules, an endomorphism is fixed by its block of total charge $0$, because the raising generator is invertible between charge blocks, and the loops formed by raising and then lowering leave only scalars in that block. On $\mathcal F^+$ the one-dimensional lowest charge block generates the module. In both cases the endomorphisms are scalars for generic parameters. This proves (ii) generically; it does not prove that the modules are irreducible. For the $a_r$ defects the triangle relation is proved for every rank without (ii), from the Yang–Baxter equation of the universal R-matrix (@prp-an-transmission). If $\mathcal W$ is a module of all of $U_q(\hat g)$, the theorem gives back the observation of @sec-triangle-relations that a particle is a transmitting defect, $\mathbb T=\check R$.

::: {#prp-sg-t-unique}
## The sine-Gordon transmission matrix from its symmetry
**[Theorem; Numerical]** Suppose $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ is not a root of unity and $y,y_d\in\mathbb C^\times$. For each offset $s\in\mathbb C$, with a fixed choice of $q^s$, the $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$-intertwiners $V(y)\otimes\mathcal W^-(y_d)\to\mathcal W^-(y_d)\otimes V(y)$ form a one-dimensional space, spanned by the matrix part of (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix). For $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ the space is spanned by the matrix with $A_n=q^n$, $D_n=q^{-n-s}$, $C_n=iq^{-1-s}(y_d/y)q^{-n}$, $B_n=iq^{-1}(y_d/y)q^n$ in the notation of the proof. Under the same assumptions, if $k_0k_1\ne1$ on $\mathcal W$, there is no non-zero intertwiner.
:::

::: {.proof}
Write $\mathbb T(v_+\otimes|n\rangle)=A_n|n\rangle\otimes v_++C_n|n+1\rangle\otimes v_-$ and $\mathbb T(v_-\otimes|n\rangle)=B_n|n-1\rangle\otimes v_++D_n|n\rangle\otimes v_-$; the $k$-equations force this form, because $q$ is not a root of unity. The $f_1$-equation on $v_-\otimes|n\rangle$, projected on $|n-2\rangle\otimes v_+$, and the $f_0$-equation on $v_+\otimes|n\rangle$, projected on $|n+2\rangle\otimes v_-$, give $B_n=qB_{n-1}$ and $C_{n+1}=q^{-1}C_n$: $C_n=c\,q^{-n}$, $B_n=b\,q^n$. The remaining projections give $\mu y(A_{n+1}-qA_n)=y_dC_n$, $\mu y(A_n-qA_{n-1})=qy_dq^{-2n-s}B_n$, $D_n=q^{2n+s}A_n$, and $\mu y(D_{n-1}-qD_n)=y_dB_n$. The first two give $b=cq^s$ and $A_n=\alpha q^n-\frac{y_dc}{\mu\kappa y}q^{-n}$. The last then requires $\alpha(q^{-3}-q)=0$, so $\alpha=0$ and everything is fixed by $c$; with $\mu\kappa=i$ this is (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix). The $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ case is the same computation with $e_j$. For the level-zero statement, with $k_0k_1=c$, the recursions for $B_n$ and $C_n$ do not involve $c$; with them, the projection of the $f_1$-equation on $|n\rangle\otimes v_-$ gives $D_n=q^{2n+s}A_n$ and that of the $f_0$-equation on $|n\rangle\otimes v_+$ gives $D_n=c^{-1}q^{2n+s}A_n$, so $A=D=0$ for $c\ne1$, and the remaining equations then force $B=C=0$. Both statements were also checked numerically, the uniqueness on windows for $s=0,0.3,1$ (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`).
:::

At a root of unity the first step fails, because the $k$-equations distinguish weights only modulo the period. For $q=e^{i\pi/3}$, so that $q^4\ne1$ but $q^6=1$, the shift $S|n\rangle=|n+1\rangle$ satisfies $S^3q^{\mathsf h}=q^{\mathsf h}S^3$ and commutes with the constant shifts $f_0$, $f_1$, so $(S^3\otimes1)\mathbb T$ is a second intertwiner, linearly independent of $\mathbb T$ (checked in the same script).

So the triangle relation, which Konik and LeClair and Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon solved as a quadratic equation [@konik_leclair1999; @bcz2005], follows from eight linear ones, as Weston and Corrigan and Zambon emphasized [@weston2010; @cz2011]. Corrigan and Zambon used the same linear method for $a_2^{(2)}$ and $a_2^{(1)}$, with Borel modules built from one and from three $q$-oscillators (@sec-t-procedure) [@cz2011].

::: {#prp-two-borels}
## The two Borel subalgebras and the two defect types
**[Proposition, sketch; numerically checked]** (1) Let $\mathcal R\in U_q(\mathfrak b^-)\hat\otimes U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ be the universal R-matrix of Part VI (@sec-reflection-algebra). Then, up to scalar functions,
$$
\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_+}(\theta)\propto P\,(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho^+)(\mathcal R),\qquad\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_-}(\theta)\propto P\,(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho^-)(\mathcal R_{21}^{-1}),
$$
with $\rho^\pm$ the Weyl modules $\mathcal W^\pm(y_d)$. The first is a series in $y_d/y$, the second in $y/y_d$. In this normalization the matrices are $q^{\pm s/2}$ times those of @prp-sg-t-unique.
(2) Weston's L-operator for $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ [@weston2010, eq. (2.9)] is written for the Part VI coproduct on $\mathcal W\otimes V$. His identification with the type-I matrix [@weston2010, eq. (4.15)] includes a transposition of both spaces (his footnote 10). Transposition maps $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$-intertwiners to $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$-intertwiners, so in a fixed reading the type-I$_-$ matrix intertwines $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$, in agreement with @sec-sg-transmission-matrix.
(3) In the basis $|a,b\rangle$ of Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon, which labels the defect by the vacua $u=2\pi a/\beta_{\rm SG}$ and $v=2\pi b/\beta_{\rm SG}$ on its two sides [@bcz2005, eqs. (3.52)–(3.59)], the map $\psi\to-\psi$, which takes type I$_-$ to type I$_+$ (@sec-sg-defect-lagrangian), sends $(a,b)$ to $(a,b')=(a,-b)$. Combined with conjugation of the outgoing soliton, it takes $\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_-}$ to a matrix that, after a diagonal change of basis, does not depend on $a+b'$ and equals $\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_+}$, with the same $y_d$, on the jump $b'-a=-(a+b)$ of the image. The offset becomes $s_+=-1-s$, and the residual freedom of the two-label basis can change it further.
(4) In the normalization of (1), the scalar factor does not depend on $s$: $\Phi(\theta-\theta_d)\,q^{-s/2}$ times the matrix of (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) satisfies defect crossing for every $s$, and it is unitary for real rapidities, real $s$ and real $\theta_d$ at the physical $|q|=1$. For complex $s$ the diagonal amplitudes $q^{\pm(n+s/2)}$ are not phases, and unitarity fails.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) $\mathcal R\Delta(a)=\Delta^{\rm op}(a)\mathcal R$ evaluated on $V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W^+$ requires only $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ on the second factor, and composing with the flip turns $\Delta^{\rm op}$ into $\Delta$ on $\mathcal W\otimes V$. $\mathcal R_{21}^{-1}$ is the other universal R-matrix of the same coproduct and lies in $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)\hat\otimes U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$. Uniqueness (@prp-sg-t-unique) gives proportionality. The leading term of $\mathcal R$ is $q^{\frac12h\otimes h}$, which on $v_\pm\otimes|n\rangle$ is $q^{\pm(2n+s)/2}$; this is the factor $q^{\pm s/2}$. (2) The map $\tau(f_j)=k_j^{-1}e_j$, $\tau(k_j)=k_j$ is an algebra anti-isomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)\to U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ with $(\tau\otimes\tau)\Delta=\Delta\tau$, so $\pi'(x)=\pi(\tau(x))^{\mathsf T}$ turns a $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$-module into a $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$-module, and $\big((\pi\otimes\pi)\Delta(\tau x)\big)^{\mathsf T}=(\pi'\otimes\pi')\Delta(x)$. Transposing $L\,(\pi\otimes\pi)\Delta(\tau x)=(\pi\otimes\pi)\Delta^{\rm op}(\tau x)\,L$ gives $L^{\mathsf T}(\pi'\otimes\pi')\Delta^{\rm op}(x)=(\pi'\otimes\pi')\Delta(x)\,L^{\mathsf T}$ for $x\in U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ (@exr-dq-transpose). This reverses the direction of intertwining; to return to the form $L_{\rm new}\Delta=\Delta^{\rm op}L_{\rm new}$ one must also reverse the tensor order, which is the passage from Weston's $\mathcal W\otimes V$ to the book's $V\otimes\mathcal W$. (3) $\psi\to-\psi$ maps $(a,b)$ to $(a,-b)$, so it exchanges the jump $b-a$ with $-(a+b)$; the rest is the computation described below. (4) @exr-sgd-crossing reduces crossing to $\Phi(\theta)\Phi(\theta+i\pi)(1+Y^2)=q^{-s}$. Multiplying $\mathbb T$ by $q^{-s/2}$ multiplies one side of crossing by $q^{-s/2}$ and the other, which involves $\mathbb T^{-1}$, by $q^{s/2}$, so the condition becomes the one for $s=0$. This is algebraic and holds for complex $s$; unitarity uses $|q^{s}|=1$, hence real $s$.
:::

All four parts were checked numerically (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`): (1) through the Khoroshkin–Tolstoy formula of @sec-universal-r-affine, with relative error $10^{-7}$ at $x=0.02$ scaling as $x^4$, and the normalization constant tending to $q^{-s/2}$; (2) by verifying that Weston's (2.9) intertwines his $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ in Part VI conventions (residual $10^{-16}$) and that its transpose at his $\zeta=iy/y_d$ has the gauge invariants of the $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ matrix, $A_{n+1}/A_n=q^{-1}$, $D_n/A_n=q^{2n+s}$, $C_nB_{n+1}/(A_nD_{n+1})=-(y/y_d)^2$, with his $j=-n$ and $r_0=q^s$; (3) by carrying out the map on a two-label window: after the gauge $q^{m(m+1)/2-nm}$, with $n=(b'-a)/2$ and $m=(a+b')/2$ the labels of the image, the amplitudes no longer depend on $m$ and have the invariants of the $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ matrix, $A_{n+1}/A_n=q$, $D_n/A_n=q^{-2n-s_+}$, $C_nB_{n+1}/(A_nD_{n+1})=-(y_d/y)^2$; (4) for $s=0.3$ and $1$, with residuals $10^{-9}$, while crossing fails without $q^{-s/2}$. Part (3) explains why the type-I$_+$ matrix is not simply $(1\otimes C)\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_-}$ with the same labels: with one label that matrix does not even conserve the charge, and the conserved charge of the image is the other label $a+b$ of the original defect. It is the quantum form of the classical statement $z_{{\rm I}_+}=-z_{{\rm I}_-}$ (@sec-sg-defect-lagrangian).

## The universal R-matrix and L-operators {#sec-universal-r-affine}

**The Khoroshkin–Tolstoy formula.** Write $\alpha=\alpha_1$ and $\delta=\alpha_0+\alpha_1$. The positive roots of $\widehat{sl}_2$ are $\alpha+k\delta$, $k\delta$ and $(\delta-\alpha)+k\delta$, and Khoroshkin and Tolstoy built the universal R-matrix as an ordered product over them, with root vectors defined by $q$-commutators [@khoroshkin_tolstoy1991; @tolstoy_khoroshkin1992]. In the conventions of Part VI the root vectors in $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ are $e_\alpha=e_1$, $e_{\delta-\alpha}=e_0$, $e'_\delta=e_1e_0-q^2e_0e_1$ and
$$
e_{\alpha+k\delta}=\frac{e_{\alpha+(k-1)\delta}e'_\delta-e'_\delta e_{\alpha+(k-1)\delta}}{[2]},\qquad e_{(\delta-\alpha)+k\delta}=\frac{e'_\delta e_{(\delta-\alpha)+(k-1)\delta}-e_{(\delta-\alpha)+(k-1)\delta}e'_\delta}{[2]},
$$
and those in $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ are $f_\alpha=f_1$, $f_{\delta-\alpha}=f_0$, $f'_\delta=f_0f_1-q^{-2}f_1f_0$, $f_{\alpha+k\delta}=[2]^{-1}(f'_\delta f_{\alpha+(k-1)\delta}-f_{\alpha+(k-1)\delta}f'_\delta)$, $f_{(\delta-\alpha)+k\delta}=[2]^{-1}(f_{(\delta-\alpha)+(k-1)\delta}f'_\delta-f'_\delta f_{(\delta-\alpha)+(k-1)\delta})$. The imaginary root vectors $e_{k\delta}$, $f_{k\delta}$ are defined from $e'_{k\delta}=e_{\alpha+(k-1)\delta}e_{\delta-\alpha}-q^2e_{\delta-\alpha}e_{\alpha+(k-1)\delta}$ and its analogue by taking logarithms of generating functions, and $e_\delta=e'_\delta$, $f_\delta=f'_\delta$. Then, on modules of level zero,
$$
\mathcal R=q^{\frac12h\otimes h}\prod_{k\ge0}^{\to}\exp_{q^{-2}}\!\big(\kappa f_{(\delta-\alpha)+k\delta}\otimes e_{(\delta-\alpha)+k\delta}\big)\;\exp\Big(\kappa\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{k}{[2k]}f_{k\delta}\otimes e_{k\delta}\Big)\prod_{k\ge0}^{\leftarrow}\exp_{q^{-2}}\!\big(\kappa f_{\alpha+k\delta}\otimes e_{\alpha+k\delta}\big),
$$ {#eq-dq-kt}
with $k_1=q^h$, $\exp_p(x)=\sum_nx^n/(n)_p!$, $(n)_p=(1-p^n)/(1-p)$, and the first product starting with $k=0$ on the left, the last ending with $k=0$ on the right. We obtained (-@eq-dq-kt) from the form of the Khoroshkin–Tolstoy formula given by Boos, Göhmann, Klümper, Nirov and Razumov [-@bgknr2014, eqs. (4.12)–(4.28)], whose algebra is the book's with $q\to q^{-1}$ and whose universal R-matrix is our $\mathcal R_{21}^{-1}$. For $U_q(sl_2)$ only the factor with $f_\alpha\otimes e_\alpha$ remains, and since $q^{n(n-1)/2}/[n]!=1/(n)_{q^{-2}}!$ it is the flip of Drinfeld's formula (-@eq-universal-r-sl2), as it must be for the opposite coproduct. The leading terms, $\mathcal R=q^{\frac12h\otimes h}(1+\kappa\sum_jf_j\otimes e_j+\dots)$, are those used in @sec-reflection-algebra.

**Truncation on spin $\frac12$.** In $V(y)$ every $f$ carries a factor $y^{-1}$, and $f_\gamma$ for a real root $\gamma$ is a multiple of $E_{21}$ or $E_{12}$, so $f_\gamma^2=0$ and each $q$-exponential is linear. Each factor is then $1+\kappa\,\pi_y(f_\gamma)\otimes e_\gamma$, a polynomial in $y^{-1}$ of the degree of the height of $\gamma$, and the imaginary factor is diagonal on $V$. Keeping the roots of height at most 3, namely $\alpha$, $\delta-\alpha$, $\delta$, $\alpha+\delta$ and $2\delta-\alpha$, gives $(\pi_y\otimes1)(\mathcal R)$ to $O(y^{-3})$ as an explicit $2\times2$ matrix with entries in $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$. On $V(y_1)\otimes V(y_2)$ it agrees with $P\check R(y_1/y_2)$ up to a scalar, with an error that falls by a factor 16 when $x=y_2/y_1$ is halved; without the imaginary factor the error is $O(x^2)$, without the roots of height 3 it is $O(x^3)$. The same holds for $\mathcal R_{21}^{-1}$ (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`).

**L-operators.** Evaluate the first factor on $V(\theta)$ and the second on a representation of the $q$-oscillator algebra through the homomorphisms of @sec-borel. With entries labelled by $v_+,v_-$, $\mathbb L=\sum_{ab}E_{ab}\otimes\mathbb L_{ab}$, the result is
$$
\mathbb L^+(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}q^{\mathsf h/2}&i\kappa x\,q^{\mathsf h/2}\mathsf a_-\\ i\kappa x\,q^{-\mathsf h/2}\mathsf a_+&q^{-\mathsf h/2}\big(1-\kappa^2x^2Z\big)\end{pmatrix},\qquad x=\frac{y_W}y,
$$
$$
\mathbb L^-(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\big(1-\kappa^2x^2q^2Z\big)q^{-\mathsf h/2}&-i\kappa x\,\mathsf a_-q^{\mathsf h/2}\\ -i\kappa x\,\mathsf a_+q^{-\mathsf h/2}&q^{\mathsf h/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad x=\frac y{y_W},
$$ {#eq-l-operator}
for $(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho)(\mathcal R)$ and $(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho)(\mathcal R_{21}^{-1})$ respectively, up to scalar functions of $x$.

::: {#prp-l-operator}
## Transmission matrices and BLZ L-operators from the universal R-matrix
**[Proposition; Numerical]** On the Weyl modules (-@eq-weyl-module) and the Fock modules (-@eq-fock-module), $(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho)(\mathcal R)$ and $(\pi_\theta\otimes\rho)(\mathcal R_{21}^{-1})$ are scalar multiples of $\mathbb L^+$ and $\mathbb L^-$ of (-@eq-l-operator). On the Weyl modules, where $Z=0$, the matrices are linear in $x$ and $P\mathbb L^\pm$ are the type-I$_\pm$ transmission matrices of @prp-two-borels. On the Fock module $\mathcal F^+$, $\mathbb L^+$ is the spin-chain counterpart of the $q$-oscillator L-operator of Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov. All of them satisfy the RTT form (-@eq-triangle-rtt) of the triangle relation.
:::

::: {.proof}
On each of these modules the intertwiner $V(\theta)\otimes\rho\to\rho\otimes V(\theta)$ is unique up to a scalar (@prp-sg-t-unique for the Weyl modules; numerically on windows for the Fock modules), and the evaluated universal R-matrix is one, so they are proportional; comparing the terms of order $x^0$ and $x^1$ with $q^{\frac12h\otimes h}(1+\kappa\sum_jf_j\otimes e_j)$ fixes the off-diagonal entries. Numerically: the closed forms (-@eq-l-operator) are the unique intertwiners on windows of the Weyl and Fock modules (residual $10^{-13}$); the truncation of (-@eq-dq-kt) agrees with them to $O(x^4)$ for both Borel subalgebras and both kinds of module; and (-@eq-triangle-rtt) holds to $10^{-15}$ (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`).
:::

Two features stand out. On a Weyl module the infinite product (-@eq-dq-kt) collapses to its linear term times a scalar: the root vectors $e_{\alpha+k\delta}$ and $e_{(\delta-\alpha)+k\delta}$ vanish there for $k\ge1$, because $e'_\delta$ acts as a scalar, and the imaginary-root factor combines with the product of the two linear factors into a scalar. The transmission matrix of a type-I defect is the simplest L-operator there is. On the Fock module the term with $Z$ survives. $\mathbb L^+$ is then the $q$-oscillator L-operator behind BLZ's Q-operators, whose conformal version is a path-ordered exponential of vertex operators [@blz1999, eq. (3.10)], and it has the form of Weston's $L^{(r)}$ with $r_1r_2=0$, the case in which his module is a $q$-oscillator module [@weston2010, eq. (2.9)]. Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov use the coproduct $\delta(x_i)=x_i\otimes1+q^{-h_i}\otimes x_i$ for their $x_i$ [@blz1999, eq. (2.6)], so their Borel subalgebra $B_-$, generated by the $x_i$, is the book's $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ with $q\to q^{-1}$. The two Borel subalgebras play symmetric roles; which one is called $\mathfrak b^+$ is a convention, and the physical content is in (1) of @prp-two-borels: the type-I$_-$ defect of the Lagrangian of @sec-sg-defect-lagrangian is the one whose transmission matrix is a series in $y/y_d$.

**The classical limit.** On a Weyl module put $U=q^{\mathsf h/2}$ and $W_\pm=q^{\mp\mathsf h/2}\kappa\mathsf a_\pm q^{\mp\mathsf h/2}$. Then
$$
UW_\pm=q^{\pm1}W_\pm U,\qquad W_+W_-=W_-W_+=1,\qquad \mathbb L^-(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}U^{-1}&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}\Big[1-ix\big(E_{21}\otimes W_++E_{12}\otimes W_-\big)\Big],\quad x=\frac y{y_d}.
$$ {#eq-dq-weyl-l}
The type-I$_-$ defect matrix of sine-Gordon theory, the case $r=1$ of the formula of @sec-defect-lax, is, in the basis $(v_+,v_-)$ in which $E_{-\alpha_1}=E_{21}$ and $E_{-\alpha_0}=E_{12}$,
$$
L_d(\lambda)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{b(\phi-\psi)/2\sqrt2}&0\\0&e^{-b(\phi-\psi)/2\sqrt2}\end{pmatrix}\Big[1+\frac\sigma\lambda\big(e^{b\phi/\sqrt2}E_{21}+e^{-b\phi/\sqrt2}E_{12}\big)\Big]\quad\text{at }x=0 .
$$
The two have the same structure under $U^{-1}\leftrightarrow e^{b(\phi-\psi)/2\sqrt2}$, $W_\pm\leftrightarrow e^{\pm b\phi/\sqrt2}$ and $-ix\leftrightarrow\sigma/\lambda$: the diagonal entries are exponentials of the jump, which is the defect charge, and the off-diagonal entries exponentials of the field at the defect, which shift it. The algebra matches too. With the bracket $\{\phi(0),\psi(0)\}=-1$ of the type-I$_-$ defect (-@eq-dc-defect-bracket), $u=e^{-b(\phi-\psi)/2\sqrt2}$ and $w_\pm=e^{\pm b\phi/\sqrt2}$ satisfy $\{u,w_\pm\}=\pm\frac{b^2}4uw_\pm$ and $w_+w_-=1$, a Poisson algebra of Weyl type, and (-@eq-dq-weyl-l) is its quantization, $UW_\pm=\hat q^{\pm1}W_\pm U$ with $\hat q=e^{i\hbar b^2/4}$ to first order in $\hbar$. Since $\mathbb L^-$ solves the RTT relation for every $q$ (checked for $q=e^{0.05i}$ and $e^{0.6i}$), its limit $q\to1$ is a classical L-operator, with a Sklyanin bracket of the form of @prp-defect-involution. So the Weyl-module L-operator quantizes $L_d$, the Weyl module is the quantized algebra of functions of the defect values, and the inverse L-operators of (-@eq-dq-defect-operator) below are the quantum counterpart of $L_d^{-1}$ in the classical defect monodromy (-@eq-defect-monodromy). The Borel subalgebra is the same on both sides: $L_d$ of type I$_-$ is polynomial in $\sigma/\lambda$, which grows with $\theta-\theta_d$, as $\mathbb L^-$ is a series in $y/y_d$ (`textbook_code/defect_universal_r.py`, by hand for the Poisson brackets). The correspondence is one of structure, not of parameters. The deformation parameter of this quantization, $\hat q=e^{-i\hbar\beta_{\rm SG}^2/8}$ at imaginary coupling, tends to 1 as $\beta_{\rm SG}\to0$, while the $q$ of the soliton symmetry, $e^{-8\pi^2i/\beta_{\rm SG}^2}$, does not, and the spectral parameter is $e^{\theta-\theta_d}$ classically and $e^{\lambda(\theta-\theta_d)}$ in the quantum theory. The same is true in the bulk, where the classical r-matrix of the Lax pair is a function of $e^\theta$ while the soliton $\check R$ is a function of $e^{\lambda\theta}$.

## Defect operators and Q-operators {#sec-q-operators}

**BLZ's T- and Q-operators.** In conformal field theory with $c=13-6(\beta^2+\beta^{-2})$, Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov defined the operators $T_j(\lambda)$ as traces, over the spin-$j$ representation of $U_q(sl_2)$, of a path-ordered exponential of vertex operators of a chiral free field: a monodromy matrix of the chiral theory [@blz1996]. Replacing the spin-$j$ representation by a representation $\rho_\pm$ of the $q$-oscillator algebra, with the twist $e^{\pm2\pi iP\mathsf h}$, whose traces converge for $\operatorname{Im}P>0$ (respectively $<0$) and are continued analytically to other momenta [@blz1997, after eq. (2.29)], they defined $A_\pm(\lambda)$ and the Q-operators $Q_\pm(\lambda)=\lambda^{\pm2P/\beta^2}A_\pm(\lambda)$ [@blz1997, eqs. (2.29), (2.38)]. They commute with each other and with all $T_j$, and satisfy Baxter's TQ relation and the quantum Wronskian [@blz1997, eqs. (2.41)–(2.42)]:
$$
T(\lambda)Q_\pm(\lambda)=Q_\pm(q\lambda)+Q_\pm(q^{-1}\lambda),\qquad Q_+(q^{\frac12}\lambda)Q_-(q^{-\frac12}\lambda)-Q_+(q^{-\frac12}\lambda)Q_-(q^{\frac12}\lambda)=2i\sin2\pi P ,
$$
with $T=T_{1/2}$ and their $q=e^{i\pi\beta^2}$. The mechanism is representation theory of the Borel subalgebra: the product $Q_+Q_-$ is the trace over the tensor product of two $q$-oscillator modules, which is related to a Verma module of the Borel subalgebra, and this gives $2i\sin(2\pi P)T_j$ as a quantum Wronskian [@blz1997, eqs. (2.43)–(2.45)]. The Yang–Baxter relation behind the commutativity was proved from the universal R-matrix in [@blz1999]. Rossi and Weston constructed a generalized Q-operator for the vertex models of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ from the most general Borel module of this type [@rossi_weston2002]. Hernandez and Jimbo defined, for every untwisted quantum affine algebra, the prefundamental representations of the Borel subalgebra, infinite-dimensional modules in a category $\mathcal O$; for $\widehat{sl}_2$ the $q$-oscillator Fock modules are of this kind [@hernandez_jimbo2012]. Frenkel and Hernandez showed that Baxter's relations are relations in the Grothendieck ring of that category, which gives TQ relations for all untwisted quantum affine algebras and a description of the spectra of transfer matrices in terms of Q-operators [@frenkel_hernandez2015].

**Defect operators on the circle.** Put $N$ solitons of rapidities $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N$ on a circle, an inhomogeneous spin chain on $V(\theta_1)\otimes\dots\otimes V(\theta_N)$, with the bulk transfer matrix
$$
t_\omega(\theta)=\mathrm{Tr}_a\big[\omega^{h_a}R_{aN}(\theta-\theta_N)\cdots R_{a1}(\theta-\theta_1)\big],\qquad R=P\check R ,
$$
twisted by $\omega^{h_a}$ as in @prp-bloch-sectors. A defect wound around the circle, as in @sec-defect-circle, crosses each soliton once, and the defect state propagates along it. Its operator is a trace over $\mathcal W$ of a product of L-operators,
$$
\mathcal D_\omega(\theta_d)=\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal W}\big[\omega^{h_{\mathcal W}}\,\mathbb L_{N\mathcal W}(\theta_N-\theta_d)^{-1}\cdots\mathbb L_{1\mathcal W}(\theta_1-\theta_d)^{-1}\big],
$$ {#eq-dq-defect-operator}
with $\mathbb L$ normalized as in (-@eq-l-operator). With the scalar factors restored, defect unitarity (-@eq-defect-unitarity) identifies this orientation with transmission from right to left; in the scalar-free normalization used here, $\mathbb L^{-1}$ is its matrix part, after the flip. The order and the inverses are fixed by the train argument below; the product $\mathbb L_N\cdots\mathbb L_1$ without inverses does not commute with $t_\omega$.

::: {#prp-defect-transfer}
## Defect operators commute
**[Proposition, sketch; numerically checked]** (1) For a Fock module, at $|q|=1$, $|\omega|<1$ and away from spectral poles, the trace (-@eq-dq-defect-operator) converges absolutely. The operators $\mathcal D_\omega(\theta_d)$ commute with each other for different $\theta_d$ and with $t_\omega(\theta)$ for all $\theta$, whenever the auxiliary intertwining and trace manipulations of the proof are defined: they are Q-operators of the inhomogeneous chain. (2) For the bilateral Weyl module $\mathcal W^-$ of the type-I$_-$ defect the trace has no convergent twist. In the sector of soliton charge $m=\sum_j\sigma_j$, $\langle n|M|n\rangle=q^{mn}\langle0|M|0\rangle$ for the product $M$ in (-@eq-dq-defect-operator), so the trace is the series $\omega^s\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}(\omega^2q^m)^n$, a formal multiplicative delta function supported at $\omega^2=q^{-m}$ (or a distribution in $\omega$ when $|\omega^2q^m|=1$), times
$$
\mathcal D(\theta_d)=\langle0|\,\mathbb L_{N\mathcal W}(\theta_N-\theta_d)^{-1}\cdots\mathbb L_{1\mathcal W}(\theta_1-\theta_d)^{-1}|0\rangle .
$$
The operators $\mathcal D(\theta_d)$ commute with each other, and in the sector of charge $m$ with $t_\omega(\theta)$ for $\omega=\pm q^{-m/2}$. In the neutral sector the twist is trivial. For $\mathcal W^+$ the exponent is $-mn$, and the formal support is $\omega^2=q^m$.
:::

::: {.proof}
By (-@eq-triangle-rtt) with spaces $a$, $j$, $\mathcal W$, $R_{aj}X\mathbb L_j=\mathbb L_jXR_{aj}$ with $X=\mathbb L_{a\mathcal W}(\theta-\theta_d)$, so $XR_{aj}\mathbb L_j^{-1}=\mathbb L_j^{-1}R_{aj}X$. Then $t_\omega\mathcal D_\omega=\mathrm{Tr}_{a\mathcal W}[\Omega\,R_{aN}\mathbb L_N^{-1}\cdots R_{a1}\mathbb L_1^{-1}]$, with $\Omega=\omega^{h_a}\omega^{h_{\mathcal W}}$, which commutes with $X$ by charge conservation. Inserting $X^{-1}X$ and moving $X$ through the product site by site turns each $R_{aj}\mathbb L_j^{-1}$ into $\mathbb L_j^{-1}R_{aj}$, and cyclicity of the trace removes $X$ at the end. This needs a trace-class product, which the twist provides for a Fock module at $|q|=1$, where the matrix elements are bounded in $n$. Two defect operators commute by the same argument with an intertwiner of $\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal W'$; such intertwiners exist as formal series [@weston2010, eqs. (2.11)–(2.13)]. For $\mathcal W^-$, a shift of $n$ multiplies the entries of $\mathbb L^-$ in the column of $v_\pm$ by $q^{\mp1}$, and the rows of its inverse by $q^{\pm1}$, which gives the factorization; for $\mathcal W^+$ the factors are inverted. The bilateral expression must be read as a formal twisted trace. On its support the auxiliary shift factors cancel, which is the algebraic content of the train argument; it does not define an ordinary convergent trace, while the matrix element $\mathcal D$ is well defined on its own. Numerically, with $N=4$ and random rapidities (`textbook_code/defect_transfer.py`): the Fock trace changes by $5\times10^{-8}$ when the window grows from $n\le40$ to $n\le80$ at $|\omega|=0.8$; the commutators vanish to $10^{-15}$; the controls (another twist, products without inverses, and for the Weyl module the untwisted $t$ in a sector with $m\ne0$) fail at order 1. The factorization is also checked for $\mathcal W^+$, with the exponent $-mn$.
:::

So the statement of @sec-defect-circle, that defect operators are transfer matrices with auxiliary space $\mathcal W$, holds with two precisions: the product is that of the inverse L-operators for the transfer matrix $t_\omega$ above, and for the Weyl modules of the Lagrangian defects the twist is tied to the charge sector. A Weyl-module trace with an arbitrary twist is not defined, and nothing in this chapter depends on untwisted traces converging.

The formal delta factor and its removal have a direct antecedent. Rossi and Weston found that the matrix elements of their Q-operator over a bilateral oscillator module contain $\delta(q^k)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}q^{kj}$, divided it out, and identified the remaining matrix in the homogeneous six-vertex case with Baxter's Q-matrix [@rossi_weston2002, Sec. 4.3, eqs. (5.5), (5.9)–(5.10)]. They checked its TQ relation in the neutral sector up to $N=10$, found it in charged sectors only at $q^n=1$, and proved mutual commutation [@rossi_weston2002, eqs. (5.11)–(5.12), App. B]. In the homogeneous case their stripped matrix has the closed form of our $\mathcal D$, a product of single-site factors times a power of $q$ given by an antisymmetric form in the input and output signs, with $q\to q^{-1}$ and up to scalar and gauge conventions. The sector twist $\omega=q^{-m/2}$ plays the role of their condition $q^n=1$; the inhomogeneous inverse-L normalization and this twist would have to be compared with their construction in detail before any novelty is assigned to the functional relation below.

**TQ relations.** For the Fock module we find, with no fitted constant,
$$
t_\omega\Big(\theta_F+\frac{i\pi}{2\lambda}\Big)\mathcal Q_s(y_F)=q^{N/2}\,\mathcal Q_{s+1}(qy_F)+\prod_{j=1}^N\frac{qz_j^2+q^{-1}}{q^{1/2}(z_j^2+1)}\,\mathcal Q_{s-1}(q^{-1}y_F),\qquad z_j=\frac{y_j}{y_F},
$$ {#eq-dq-tq-fock}
where $\mathcal Q_s(y_F)$ is (-@eq-dq-defect-operator) on $\mathcal F^+(y_F)$ with offset $s$, $y_F=e^{\lambda\theta_F}$ and $y_j=e^{\lambda\theta_j}$. The relation holds to $10^{-15}$ for $N=4$, the shifts $q^{\pm2}$ fail, and the denominators come from the inverses in (-@eq-dq-defect-operator) (`textbook_code/defect_transfer.py`). It is the spin-chain form of BLZ's TQ relation. Its structure, two Q-operators at $q^{\pm1}y_F$ with the offset shifted by $\pm1$, is that of a short exact sequence of Borel modules with $\mathcal F(y_F)\otimes V$ in the middle, as Weston found for his modules [@weston2010, Sec. 2.4.1]; we have not written out the sequence in the conventions of this chapter.

::: {#cnj-defect-tq}
## TQ relation for the Weyl defect operator
**[Numerical]** for $N\le6$; **[Conjecture]** for all $N$. In the sector of charge $m$, with $\omega_m=q^{-m/2}$ and $z_j=y_j/y_d$,
$$
t_{\omega_m}\Big(\theta_d+\frac{i\pi}{2\lambda}\Big)\,\mathcal D(y_d)=q^{-N/2}\,\mathcal D(qy_d)+\prod_{j=1}^N\frac{q^{1/2}(qz_j^2+q^{-1})}{z_j^2+1}\,\mathcal D(q^{-1}y_d),
$$
for the type-I$_-$ defect operator $\mathcal D$ of @prp-defect-transfer, at any $s$.
:::

For $N=2,\dots,6$ and random rapidities the relation holds to $10^{-14}$ in every sector, with the coefficients above and no fit; the shifts $q^{\pm2}$ fail. For $N=4$ the test is not empty even without the predicted coefficients: in the neutral sector, of dimension 6, the operators $\mathcal D(y_d)$ span a three-dimensional space, while two coefficients are available. For $N\le3$ that space has dimension at most 2, and only the predicted values of the coefficients are tested (`textbook_code/defect_transfer.py`). The coefficients are those of (-@eq-dq-tq-fock) with $q^{1/2}\to q^{-1/2}$ and without the shift of $s$, which for a Weyl module changes $\mathcal D$ only by a scalar in each sector.

**Reading the relation as the defect bootstrap.** Since $y_d\to-y_d$ is a change of basis of $\mathcal W$ that leaves $\langle0|\cdot|0\rangle$ unchanged, and $q^{\pm1}y_d=-e^{\lambda(\theta_d\mp i\pi)}$, the right-hand side relates the defect at $\theta_d$ to the defects at $\theta_d\mp i\pi$, which are the odd-sector defects of @sec-sg-defect-spectrum. On the left, the bulk transfer matrix is evaluated at $\theta_d+\frac{i\pi}{2\lambda}$, and $\theta_d-\frac{i\pi}{2\lambda}$ (also allowed, since $y\to-y$ is a symmetry) is the resonance $\theta_P$. So the spectral shifts of the TQ relation agree with the odd-sector shifts of the defect bootstrap of @sec-sg-defect-spectrum, which suggests reading the relation as its scalar-free operator counterpart: fusing the defect with a soliton at the resonance rapidity gives the excited defects at $\theta_d\mp i\pi$, which ch. 37 found by restricting $\check R_{23}\mathbb T_{12}$ and $\mathbb T_{23}\check R_{12}$, and the two odd defects play the roles of BLZ's $Q(q^{\pm1}\lambda)$. To identify the two terms with the image and the kernel of the resonance fusion one would have to write out the exact sequence of Weston's Sec. 2.4.1 in these conventions and restore the scalar transmission factors; the parameter identities alone do not establish that identification.

::: {#prp-defect-twist-limit}
## Defects far from the particles' rapidities
**[Proposition; numerically checked]** Let $\mathbb T$ be the type-I$_-$ transmission matrix (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) with the scalar factor (-@eq-sgd-scalar), with $\lambda>0$, real rapidities and real $s$. (1) As $\theta-\theta_d\to-\infty$,
$$
\mathbb T(\theta)\,(v_\pm\otimes|n\rangle)\to q^{s/2}\,q^{\mp(2n+s)/2}\,|n\rangle\otimes v_\pm ,
$$
with corrections of order $e^{\min(1,\lambda)(\theta-\theta_d)}$. On each eigenspace $\mathbb C|n\rangle$ of the defect charge this is $q^{s/2}$ times the twist defect of @prp-twist-defect with $e^{i\alpha_n}=q^{-(2n+s)/2}$, $q^{1/2}=e^{i\pi(1-\lambda)/2}$. (2) Consequently the defect Bethe–Yang transfer matrices $T_j$ of @sec-defect-circle tend, on each $|n\rangle$, to $q^{s/2}$ times the Bloch-twisted transfer matrices of @prp-bloch-sectors with $\alpha=\alpha_n$, and the defect operator $\mathcal D$ of @prp-defect-transfer tends to $q^{ms/2}$, a function of the charge alone. (3) As $\theta-\theta_d\to+\infty$, $\mathbb T$ becomes proportional to $v_+\otimes|n\rangle\mapsto-iq^{-n}|n+1\rangle\otimes v_-$, $v_-\otimes|n\rangle\mapsto-iq^{n+s}|n-1\rangle\otimes v_+$: charge conjugation of the soliton, the invertible line of $\phi\to-\phi$, dressed by a shift of the defect charge that keeps the total charge conserved.
:::

::: {.proof}
The entries $C_n$, $B_n$ of (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) are of order $Y=e^{\lambda(\theta-\theta_d)}$ relative to $A_n$, $D_n$, and $\Phi(\theta)\to1$ as $\theta\to-\infty$: its modulus is $(1+Y^2)^{-1/2}$, and the Gamma-function ratio in (-@eq-sgd-scalar) tends to $e^{-i\pi(1+\lambda)/4}$, which cancels the explicit prefactor $e^{i\pi(1+\lambda)/4}$ (the modulus alone would not determine this limit). Numerically the approach is exponential in $\theta-\theta_d$. $A_n=q^{-n}$ and $D_n=q^{n+s}$ are $q^{s/2}q^{\mp(2n+s)/2}$. For (2), insert the limit into $T_j$; the twist acts on particle $j$ when it crosses the defect, which is the common seam of @prp-twist-defect. For $\mathcal D$, the inverse of the diagonal limit, in the normalization of @prp-two-borels, is $q^{\pm s/2}$ on $v_\pm\otimes|0\rangle$, and the product over the solitons is $q^{ms/2}$. (3) is the same with the roles of the entries exchanged. Checked in `textbook_code/defect_transfer.py`: the error falls by $e^{3}$ when $\theta-\theta_d$ goes from $-3$ to $-6$, the limiting $T_1$ equals the twisted one to $10^{-15}$, and the limits of (2) and (3) are approached at the expected rates.
:::

The twist angles depend on the sign of $q$, and like every statement about that sign they refer to the book's fixed exchange and crossing conventions. A Klein-factor redefinition, which multiplies the soliton and antisoliton operators of (-@eq-defect-zf) by $\kappa_\pm$ and the defect operator of charge label $n$ by $J^n$, with $\kappa_\pm^2=1$, $\kappa_+\kappa_-=-\kappa_-\kappa_+$ and $J=\kappa_+\kappa_-$, maps the even-sector matrix $\mathbb T(q)$ to $\mathbb T(-q)=\mathbb T(q)(1\otimes\Pi_{\mathcal W})$, $\Pi_{\mathcal W}|n\rangle=(-1)^n|n\rangle$, and so shifts $\alpha_n$ by $\pi n$. It changes the bulk exchange amplitudes and the crossing pairing at the same time, as in @sec-crossing-sign, so it is not a change of the one-particle basis; in the conventions of this book crossing selects $q=-e^{-i\pi\lambda}$ (@prp-sg-transmission), and (4) of @prp-two-borels holds there.

The proposition is the bridge between the two kinds of line in @sec-defect-scattering. A defect at a rapidity far above the particles' rapidities acts on them only through the phase $q^{\mp(2n+s)/2}$ of its stored charge: a superposition, over the defect charge $n$, of invertible twist lines, which is the Bloch sector structure of @prp-bloch-sectors. Far below, it converts each particle into its conjugate while shifting the defect charge, as in (3); this limit acts on the combined particle–defect space, not on the particles alone. In between, it converts particles with the amplitude $Y$ and has the resonance of @sec-sg-defect-spectrum. At the conformal point this is (-@eq-dq-massless-defect): left-movers pass with a phase, right-movers are conjugated.

## Boundaries and defects compared {#sec-defect-boundary-dictionary}

The table collects the algebraic structures of Part VII and of this chapter. The last column records the status of the defect entries; the third column, the defect seen as a boundary of the doubled theory of @sec-doubling-trick, is the subject of @sec-defect-boundary, where it is settled.

| | Boundary (Part VII) | Defect (this chapter) | Defect, doubled (ch. 42) | Status of the defect entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Symmetry | coideal $B\subset U_q(\hat g)$, $\Delta(B)\subset U_q(\hat g)\otimes B$ (@sec-coideal) | Hopf subalgebra $U_q(\mathfrak b^\pm)$ (@sec-borel) | left coideal of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, $U=U_q(\hat g)$ (-@eq-dbd-coproduct): invertible lines and the transparent defect, a twisted diagonal $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ (@prp-diagonal-coideal); type-I$_\mp$ jump defect, $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))$ and $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\pm))$ on two module structures of $\mathcal W$, and no twisted diagonal (@cnj-twisted-diagonal, @prp-diagonal-borel); for type I$_-$ of $a_r^{(1)}$, $\tau$ becomes the rotation $\pi$ (@prp-dpt-doubled) | Borel intertwining established for the stated generic modules; the Weyl module does not extend to $U_q(\hat g)$ (exact argument); no classification of all defect symmetries is claimed; doubled: [Numerical] (sine-Gordon; $a_2$, $a_3$), with the second module structure and the obstruction by hand |
| Module of the line | one-dimensional (ground state), boundary bound states | infinite-dimensional: Weyl module (type I), generalized oscillator (type II) | $\mathcal W$ as a dynamical boundary module of $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))$ (@sec-jump-coideal) | [Established] [@weston2010; @cz2011] |
| Matrix | $K(\theta):V(\theta)\to\bar V(-\theta)$ | $\mathbb T(\theta):V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W\to\mathcal W\otimes V(\theta)$ | $K=\begin{pmatrix}0&\bar{\mathbb T}P\\P\mathbb T&0\end{pmatrix}$ (-@eq-doubled-k) | |
| Linear equation | (-@eq-k-intertwiner) | (-@eq-borel-intertwiner) | intertwiner of the coideal on $(V\oplus V')\otimes\mathcal W$; for $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))$ it is (-@eq-borel-intertwiner) | |
| Quadratic equation | reflection equation, @thm-k-reflection | triangle relation, @thm-t-triangle | reflection equation of the doubled theory (@prp-doubling) | [Theorem] under hypotheses (i)–(iii); (ii) checked exactly for the generic Weyl and Fock modules |
| Quadratic algebra | reflection-equation algebra, $\mathcal B=\bar LKL$ (-@eq-b-matrix) | Yang–Baxter (RTT) algebra, $\mathbb L^+=(\pi\otimes\rho^+)(\mathcal R)$, $\mathbb L^-=(\pi\otimes\rho^-)(\mathcal R_{21}^{-1})$ up to scalars (-@eq-l-operator) | reflection-equation algebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$; its off-diagonal part is the RTT algebra of $\mathbb L=P\mathbb T$ with $\mathbb L^{-1}$ adjoined (@sec-jump-coideal) | [Proposition; Numerical] |
| Universal object | universal K-matrix [@balagovic_kolb2019; @appel_vlaar2022] | universal R-matrix [@khoroshkin_tolstoy1991] | diagonal type: quasi-K-matrix = Lusztig's quasi-R-matrix twisted by $\omega\otimes1$ [@bao_wang2018b] (finite type); for $\hat g$ the universal R-matrix plays this role (@sec-diagonal-qsp) | |
| Operator on the circle | boundary state; double-row transfer matrix | Fock trace: Q-operator; bilateral Weyl module: the sector matrix element $\mathcal D$ (@prp-defect-transfer) | boundary state of the doubled theory = defect operator [@bajnok_george2006] | [Proposition, sketch; Numerical] |
| Functional relations | boundary T-systems, fusion of boundaries | TQ relations, T-systems (@cnj-defect-tq) [@runkel2008] | fusion onto boundaries, $K_{\rm f}=\bar{\mathbb T}(1\otimes K)\mathbb T$ (@prp-defect-fusion-k) | Fock: [Numerical]; Weyl: [Numerical] for $N\le6$ |
| Classical limit | fixed points of an involution (@sec-symmetric-pairs) | $L_d$ with $\{L_d\overset\otimes,L_d\}=[r,L_d\otimes L_d]$ (@prp-defect-involution), quantized by $\mathbb L^-$ on a Weyl module (-@eq-dq-weyl-l) | boundary K-matrix dressed by $L_d^{-1}$ (-@eq-dbd-dressed-k), @prp-fused-bdg | [Numerical] for independent defect values; the relation to the full equal-time field theory needs a separate reduction; the quantization: by hand and numerically |

: Algebraic structures of boundaries and defects. {#tbl-boundary-defect-algebra}

The two quadratic algebras are worth writing next to each other. With $\mathbb L_i$ the L-operator in the auxiliary space $i$ and $\mathcal B_i$ the $\mathcal B$-matrix of (-@eq-b-matrix),
$$
R_{12}\,\mathbb L_1\,\mathbb L_2=\mathbb L_2\,\mathbb L_1\,R_{12},\qquad\qquad R_{12}\,\mathcal B_1\,R_{21}\,\mathcal B_2=\mathcal B_2\,R_{12}\,\mathcal B_1\,R_{21},
$$
up to the spectral parameters: the Yang–Baxter algebra of the defect, whose representations on $\mathcal W$ are the transmission matrices, and the reflection-equation algebra of the boundary, which @prp-b-coideal embeds into $U_q(\hat g)$ as a coideal. The first is a bialgebra and the second only a comodule algebra, which is the difference between a line that particles cross and one they bounce off. How the Yang–Baxter algebra of the defect sits in the reflection-equation algebra of the doubled theory, and which coideal of $U_q(\hat g)\otimes U_q(\hat g)$ corresponds to it, is the question of @sec-jump-coideal.

## Exercises {#sec-defect-qg-exercises}

::: {#exr-dq-verlinde}
Using the modular matrix of the Ising model, compute the eigenvalues of $D_\varepsilon$ and $D_\sigma$ on the three sectors and verify $D_\sigma^2=D_{\mathbb 1}+D_\varepsilon$. Show that the space of states on a circle cut by $\sigma$ is $\bigoplus_{i,j}N_{\sigma i}^{\;j}R_i\otimes\bar R_j$ and list its primary states. Repeat the calculation for a circle cut by the $\varepsilon$-line. In which of the two twisted spaces does a primary with $(h,\bar h)=(\frac1{16},\frac1{16})$ occur, and how does it represent the disorder field $\mu$?
:::

::: {#exr-dq-chiral-defect}
Derive (-@eq-dq-massless-defect) from (-@eq-sg-defect-conditions) at $m_0=0$. Show that at the defect $\phi+\psi$ depends only on $t+x$ and $\phi-\psi$ only on $t-x$, so that the two terms of (-@eq-sg-defect-potential) are chiral defect fields of opposite chiralities. How do their couplings change under a boost by $\vartheta$, and what does this say about $\theta_d$?
:::

::: {#exr-dq-oscillator}
Assume that $q$ is generic. Show from (-@eq-q-oscillator) that $\mathsf a_-\mathsf a_+-\kappa^{-2}=q^2Z$ and $Z\mathsf a_\pm=q^{\pm2}\mathsf a_\pm Z$. Verify that (-@eq-weyl-module) and (-@eq-fock-module) are representations, and that in a shift module with $u_n=e_1e_0|_n$ the $q$-Serre relations reduce to $u_n-[3]u_{n+1}+[3]u_{n+2}-u_{n+3}=0$. Solve this recursion for a module in which the upward shift is nonzero, and identify the Weyl and Fock modules among the solutions; treat the Fock endpoint separately.
:::

::: {#exr-dq-hopf}
Show that $U_q(\mathfrak b^\pm)$ are Hopf subalgebras and that the coideal $B$ of (-@eq-coideal-generators) is not. Go through the proof of @thm-t-triangle with $U_q(\mathfrak b)$ replaced by a left coideal and find the step that fails. Why does the proof of @thm-k-reflection not need it?
:::

::: {#exr-dq-unique}
Write out the eight intertwining equations for $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ on $V(y)\otimes\mathcal W^-(y_d)$ and complete the proof of @prp-sg-t-unique for $q$ not a root of unity. Explain why the four-channel form need not follow from the $k$-equations at a root of unity, and construct an additional intertwiner for $q=e^{i\pi/3}$. Separately, examine the degeneracy of the recursion at $q^4=1$. Repeat for $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ and recover the matrix stated there.
:::

::: {#exr-dq-l-operator}
Evaluate $q^{\frac12h\otimes h}(1+\kappa\sum_jf_j\otimes e_j)$ on $V(y)\otimes\mathcal W^+(y_d)$ and show that, after moving the $q^{\pm h/2}$ to the right, it equals $\mathbb L^+$ of (-@eq-l-operator) with $Z=0$ exactly. Show that $e'_\delta$ is a scalar on $\mathcal W^+$, so that all higher real root vectors vanish there. Check (-@eq-triangle-rtt) for $\mathbb L^+$ directly.
:::

::: {#exr-dq-transpose}
Show that $\tau(f_j)=k_j^{-1}e_j$, $\tau(k_j)=k_j$ defines an anti-isomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)\to U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ with $(\tau\otimes\tau)\Delta=\Delta\tau$. Show that transposing $L\Delta=\Delta^{\rm op}L$ gives $L^{\mathsf T}\Delta^{\rm op}=\Delta L^{\mathsf T}$ on the transposed modules, so that the direction of intertwining is reversed. Account explicitly for the reversal from Weston's $\mathcal W\otimes V$ to the book's $V\otimes\mathcal W$, and explain how this reconciles Weston's identification of the type-I matrix with an L-operator of $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ with @sec-sg-transmission-matrix.
:::

::: {#exr-dq-weyl-trace}
Show that shifting $n$ by one multiplies the column of $v_\pm$ in $\mathbb L^-$ by $q^{\mp1}$, and deduce $\langle n|M|n\rangle=q^{mn}\langle0|M|0\rangle$. Compute $\sum_{|n|\le K}\omega^{2n}q^{mn}$ and explain in which sense, formally or as a distribution in $\omega$ on a circle, it is supported at $\omega^2=q^{-m}$; why does it not converge pointwise? What changes for $\mathcal W^+$? Then take $\theta_d\to+\infty$ in $\mathcal D$ and recover the twist operator of @prp-defect-twist-limit.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-defect-qg-notes}

Topological defects in conformal field theory, and the twisted partition functions that classify them, are due to Petkova and Zuber [-@petkova_zuber2001]; Fröhlich, Fuchs, Runkel and Schweigert identified Kramers–Wannier duality with a defect and developed the general theory [-@ffrs2004; -@ffrs2007]. Konik and LeClair introduced chiral defect perturbations and showed that they are purely transmitting [-@konik_leclair1999]. Runkel proved that perturbed topological defects satisfy T-systems [-@runkel2008] and that they give the non-local conserved charges of perturbed minimal models [-@runkel2010]; Kormos, Runkel and Watts studied their flows [-@kormos_runkel_watts2009], and Bajnok, Holló and Watts tested the Lee–Yang case against scattering theory [-@bhw2014]. The $q$-oscillator algebra and Q-operators in conformal field theory are due to Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov [-@blz1996; -@blz1997; -@blz1999]; Rossi and Weston generalized the Borel modules, and for the bilateral module isolated the formal delta factor of the trace, identified the stripped matrix with Baxter's Q-matrix and checked its TQ relation [-@rossi_weston2002]. Bajnok related the Rossi–Weston L-operator to type-I defects in spin chains [-@bajnok2006], Weston placed the sine-Gordon transmission matrices of both types in this setting [-@weston2010], and Corrigan and Zambon extended the linear method to $a_2^{(2)}$ and $a_2^{(1)}$ [-@cz2011]. The universal R-matrix of quantum affine algebras is due to Khoroshkin and Tolstoy [-@khoroshkin_tolstoy1991; -@tolstoy_khoroshkin1992]; we used the explicit form for $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ given by Boos, Göhmann, Klümper, Nirov and Razumov [-@bgknr2014]. Prefundamental representations and Baxter's relations in general are due to Hernandez and Jimbo [-@hernandez_jimbo2012] and Frenkel and Hernandez [-@frenkel_hernandez2015]. The diagonal-type quantum symmetric pairs of the third column of @tbl-boundary-defect-algebra are discussed by Bao and Wang [-@bao_wang2018b, Remark 4.10(2)]. @thm-t-triangle is the defect analogue of @thm-k-reflection. The closed forms (-@eq-l-operator) in book conventions, @prp-two-borels (2)–(4) (part (1) is a translation of the universal R-matrix conventions), the sector twist $\omega=q^{-m/2}$, the inhomogeneous charged-sector form of @cnj-defect-tq and its tentative reading as the defect bootstrap, @prp-defect-twist-limit, (-@eq-dq-massless-defect) and the quantization of $L_d$ by (-@eq-dq-weyl-l) are stated here; the factorization of the bilateral trace and the stripped matrix go back to Rossi and Weston, and the TQ mechanism to Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov and to Weston.

Corrections and clarifications to the sources made in this chapter:

- Weston calls the type-I defect algebra $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$, with the coproduct of Part VI [@weston2010, eq. (2.6)]. His identification [@weston2010, eq. (4.15)] includes a transposition (his footnote 10), and transposition exchanges the two Borel subalgebras (@exr-dq-transpose). In a fixed reading the type-I$_-$ matrix of Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon intertwines $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$, and the type-I$_+$ matrix $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$. His type-I module, $r=(r_0,0,0)$, is our Weyl module with $j=-n$ and $r_0=q^s$; his type-II modules have both $r_1,r_2\ne0$.
- Weston describes Q-operators as regularized traces of his L-operator over $W^{(r)}$ and leaves the regularization to be specified [@weston2010, Sec. 2.4.1]. For the type-I module, $r_1=r_2=0$, at $|q|=1$, the case of sine-Gordon theory, no ordinary twist makes the trace over $\mathbb Z$ converge; it factorizes into a formal series in the twist and the matrix element $\langle0|\cdot|0\rangle$ (@prp-defect-transfer), as Rossi and Weston had found for their bilateral module [@rossi_weston2002, Sec. 4.3, eqs. (5.5)–(5.10)]. This is a clarification, not an error in the existence of formal Q-operators. Twisted traces converge for the Fock modules at $|q|=1$ and $|\omega|<1$; in Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov they are defined in a complex-momentum domain and continued analytically.
- Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon's two labels $(a,b)$ [@bcz2005, eqs. (3.57)–(3.59)] are what relates the two defect types: $\psi\to-\psi$ exchanges the jump $b-a$ with $a+b$ up to sign, so $\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_+}$ is not $(1\otimes C)\mathbb T_{{\rm I}_-}$ in the original labels. Their remark that the dependence on $\nu$ can be removed in the two-label basis is the statement that the offset $s_+=-1-s$ of the image can be changed by the residual gauge freedom.
- The universal R-matrix of Boos, Göhmann, Klümper, Nirov and Razumov is written for the coproduct $\Delta(e_i)=e_i\otimes1+q^{-h_i}\otimes e_i$ [@bgknr2014, eq. (4.10)], which is that of Part VI with $q\to q^{-1}$; translated, their $\mathcal R$ is the book's $\mathcal R_{21}^{-1}$. Bazhanov, Lukyanov and Zamolodchikov's $B_-$ [@blz1999, eq. (2.6)] is likewise the book's $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ with $q\to q^{-1}$.
- Book-internal: @sec-defect-circle states that defect operators commute with the transfer matrices by the train argument. With $t_\omega$ as in @sec-q-operators, the product must be that of the inverse L-operators, and for Weyl modules the twist is fixed by the charge sector (@prp-defect-transfer). The $s$-dependence of the scalar factor found by hand in @exr-sgd-crossing is the factor $q^{-s/2}$ of the universal-R normalization, now checked numerically.
